rows.basis: Growth in gross Technical infrastructure, 203,679m − 141,852m = 61,827m, against 91,447m of purchases of property and equipment. This counts all growth in servers, network equipment and data centers, AI or not. It excludes assets not yet in service (78,592m, up from 50,597m). The Q4 2025 call's split of about 60% servers and 40% data centers and networking supports reading most of this as the compute fleet. No AI share or amount was stated.

Growth in gross Technical infrastructure, 141,852m − 112,504m = 29,348m, against 52,535m of capex. This counts all growth in servers, network and data-center assets, not only AI. Assets not yet in service (50,597m, up from 35,136m) are excluded.

Growth in gross Information technology assets (the server category before the FY2024 recategorization), 80,594m − 66,267m = 14,327m, against 32,251m of capex. Technical infrastructure at FY2023 was 112,504m, so the new category is broader and the two series are not mixed here. This counts all server and network growth, not only AI.

Growth in gross Information technology assets, 66,267m − 55,606m = 10,661m, against 31,485m of capex. This is all server and network growth in a year before the generative-AI ramp, so it overstates AI.

The Q4 2025 release guides total 2026 capex to $175–185bn "to meet customer demand". The FY2025 MD&A says investment is scaling technical infrastructure "in particular for AI". This is the whole capex, not the AI part, so no amount is attributed. Purchase commitments were $149.1bn at year-end 2025 (FY2025 10-K); that figure is not in the pack.

The Q2 2026 release says $49.6bn of net proceeds from the June 2026 stock and mandatory convertible preferred issuance will go to general corporate purposes "including capital expenditures to scale AI infrastructure and global compute". No amount is earmarked for AI.

The FY2025 MD&A and releases say "Alphabet-level activities primarily reflect expenses related to our shared AI research and development". Their cost is not in the pack. AI also shows up as depreciation of the fleet, which is not quantified as AI.
FY2024 releases say unallocated costs "primarily include AI-focused shared R&D activities, including development costs of our general AI models". No amount is in the pack.
From Q1 2023, after the segment change, unallocated corporate costs "primarily include AI-focused shared R&D activities" (Google DeepMind). No amount is in the pack.

The FY2025 MD&A says technical-infrastructure operating costs (depreciation, energy, equipment, network capacity) "are expected to significantly increase as developing and serving AI offerings require more compute power". No amount is given.
